clue.text: It's ever on the move — fidgety

indicators.note: letters that are on the move shift around, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone restless never keeps still: it's always shifting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges ITSEVER, the letters of 'It's ever' (the apostrophe adds nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: Restive and fidgety are synonyms: both describe someone restless and unable to stay still.

clue.text: Off-putting answers betraying inexperience

indicators.note: read as 'putting off', i.e. putting out of order, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A candidate's awkward replies reveal how green they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-putting' (read as 'put off', thrown into disorder) rearranges ANSWERS; 'betraying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawness is greenness, the state of being new to something and lacking experience.

clue.text: Plumb malingering!

parts.note: a sailor sounding depth swings a lead weight on a line (a plumb); the same idiom means shirking work by faking illness

explanation.surface: A two-word exclamation about pure, outright skiving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plumb' looks like an adverb meaning 'utterly'; it is the plumb line whose swung weight gives the phrase. 'Swinging the lead' is British slang for dodging work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pretending to be ill to avoid duty, which is malingering; literally it describes heaving a sounding weight.

clue.text: One has to return a Greek's letter

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the little word before it is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone must hand back a letter belonging to a Greek correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns 'to' into OT; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth character of the Greek alphabet bears this name.

clue.text: Rather late in the day for doing the ironing

definitions.meaning: the part of the day after the afternoon, towards night
making flat or level, smoothing out creases

explanation.surface: Someone saves the household pressing for the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the time before night; read as a verb form it means making level, which is what pressing clothes does.

clue.text: Pays tribute to rider about to mount

indicators.note: about means around, so the postscript letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a rider added to a letter is a postscript, PS
to mount is to go up or increase, as with raise

explanation.surface: A horseman is honoured just as he prepares to climb into the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' looks like a jockey but is an addendum to a letter; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to commend them, which is paying tribute.

clue.text: Spend a long time making the crossing

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Getting across takes ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey across water, a sea crossing.

clue.text: Presently without title

definitions.meaning: an old word for soon, in a little while
short for anonymous, with no name attached

explanation.surface: Something will shortly appear, but with no name on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic 'soon' and the abbreviation for an unnamed author share the same spelling.

clue.text: Like an instructor and the room his class trashed

indicators.note: a trashed room is wrecked and in disorder, so the four words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher's classroom has been wrecked by his pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashed' rearranges the fifteen letters of 'the room his class'; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes manner typical of a pedantic teacher or instructor.

clue.text: Refuses to work in buffets

definitions.meaning: hits or batters, as wind does

explanation.surface: Workers walk out at the station cafeterias.
explanation.definitionFit: A union walkout and hitting blows share the word.

clue.text: The referee's mum — picture that!

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, so is jokingly a whistler; possessive
mum is mother

explanation.surface: Imagine the match official's own mother!
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' is a noun, the famous 1871 painting by James McNeill Whistler; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This portrait of the artist's mother is one of the best-known American paintings.

clue.text: Extremely irritable

parts.note: playfully, 'at the extremes' is on the edge, while the whole phrase also describes someone tense

explanation.surface: Someone is very short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means nervous and tetchy, so this word fits very irritable.

clue.text: Fibre the French quarter is turning over

indicators.note: turning over means flipping round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: la is a French word for the
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Thread from the French district is being turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses LASIS as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a strong plant fibre from agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Favouring potassium as a help in the garden

parts.note: being for something is favouring it
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A chemical fertiliser is backed as good for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden fork is a tool for digging, a gardener's aid.

clue.text: Superior, being in order

parts.note: a superior is the head of a monastery, and he belongs to a religious order; the surface suggests something tidy

explanation.surface: Something is better because it is neatly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an abbey is a monastic superior within a religious order.

clue.text: Unbridled anger and the row resulting

indicators.note: unbridled means let loose and out of control, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Uncontrolled rage leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbridled' rearranges ANGER; 'and the ... resulting' are link words, with 'row' a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of hills is a line or series of them.

clue.text: Decline to hold with second-rate means of defence

indicators.note: holding something means enclosing it, so one piece contains the others

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline
and means together with
B is a second-class grade

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to back an inferior form of protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb meaning refuse, but it is a noun-like droop; 'to hold' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks filled with sand are piled up as a barrier against floods or gunfire.

clue.text: Renaissance man making use of masseur

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are used to make something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A Renaissance figure hires a massage therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderius Erasmus was a Dutch humanist scholar of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Getting a pet for small daughter in a metropolitan area

parts.note: a cat is a pet
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Buying a kitten for a little girl in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: CATFORD is a district of south-east London; 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This neighbourhood lies in the London borough of Lewisham, an urban area.

clue.text: Putting many skirts on — all red

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
to skirt is to edge, and rims are edges

explanation.surface: Someone dressing in lots of skirts is clad entirely in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like clothing but means borders; 'Putting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour is a deep red, so something wholly that colour is all red.

clue.text: In Australia running water is dear

definitions.meaning: a river in south-east Australia bears this name
a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.surface: Water flowing in Australia is expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's longest river shares its name with a word for a beloved person.

clue.text: Sublime English clown

parts.note: august means majestic or sublime

explanation.surface: A grand English entertainer in greasepaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus clown of the bumbling, red-nosed kind is called by this French term.

clue.text: Encompassed by a medico in distress

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the doctor goes inside the word for anxiety

parts.note: angst is anxiety or distress
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: Surrounded by a doctor in a troubled state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word; 'in' is the container signal, the doctor sitting after the first letter of the anxiety word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something among others is surrounded or encompassed by them.

clue.text: He'll try writing with evident hesitation

parts.note: an essay is a piece of writing
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man will attempt composition, though plainly hesitant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who essays is one who attempts something, so a person who will try.

clue.text: Fancy a little cottage beside a wood

indicators.note: only a little of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of a small cottage next to a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' picks the run straddling 'beside' and 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or thought, as in 'I have a fancy to go'.

clue.text: Sit on youngsters!

definitions.meaning: a hen sits on eggs to hatch them
a family of offspring hatched together

explanation.surface: An order to squash the children.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen incubates eggs, and the young it hatches share the same name.

clue.text: Parterre county

definitions.meaning: a formal garden laid out in ornamental flower plots
short form of Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A formal garden belonging to an English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre consists of flower plots, and the abbreviation names Bedfordshire.

clue.text: A French girl can be the making of American servicemen

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers, two of them giving the letters twice
GIs are US soldiers, two of them giving the letters twice

explanation.surface: A girl from France can be the making of US soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gigi is Colette's novella about a Parisian girl; 'can be the making of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Colette's story and the musical film is a young Parisian.

clue.text: A hot issue!

parts.note: issue as something that flows out, here molten rock from a volcano, not a contentious topic

explanation.surface: A controversial subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock pours out of a volcano, a very hot outflow.

clue.text: A matter of relative weight and particular importance

definitions.meaning: density compared with that of water
specific means particular and gravity means seriousness or importance

explanation.surface: Something is a question of comparative weight and special significance.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term is relative density, and its words also mean particular seriousness.

clue.text: Being agreeable, though drowsy

definitions.meaning: moving the head up and down in assent

explanation.surface: Someone is going along with things while half asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclining the head shows assent, and the head also drops when falling asleep.

clue.text: Drink with cold woman pedagogue

parts.note: tea is a drink
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A frosty woman academic has a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or educator.
